Compute the Response Adjustment for One Fit Group

Source: R/response_adjustment.R
compute_response_adjustment.Rd

Determines the blank-subtraction value and the log-scale offset that preprocess_standards() and transform_sample_response() apply, so the standards, controls and test samples of a fit group share one response axis.

Usage

compute_response_adjustment(
  standards,
  response_variable,
  is_log_response,
  samples = NULL,
  controls = NULL,
  blank_data = NULL,
  blank_option = "ignored",
  include_col = "included",
  delta = 0.001
)

Arguments

standards

Data frame of standards (raw response).

response_variable

Character. Response column name (same in all frames).

is_log_response

Logical. Offset is only applied on the log path.

samples, controls

Data frames or NULL. Test samples and controls (raw response). Rows flagged excluded by include_col are ignored.

blank_data

Data frame or NULL. Blanks (only for the subtraction value).

blank_option

Character. See perform_blank_operation().

include_col

Character. Logical include/mask column; absent = all rows.

delta

Numeric. Margin above zero for the smallest value. Default 0.001 (response units).

Value

Named list: blank_value, blank_centre, offset, delta, n_nonpositive (values <= 0 in the offset set), min_response, is_log_response, blank_option.

Details

Offset rule (log response only). If every included standard, control and test-sample response (after any blank subtraction) is > 0, the offset is 0 and nothing changes. If any is <= 0, offset = -min + delta is added to every value, so the smallest lands delta above zero. Blanks never decide the offset. The offset is recorded with the fit.
